units.source_text: 竹林外围都是柱子，进到约莫半町多的地方，才看到一片稀稀拉拉的杉树。

en.t: The outer edge of the bamboo grove was all pillars, and only after going in a little more than half a cho did I see a sparse stand of cedars.

units.source_text: ——这正是我实施计划的好地方。

en.t: This was exactly the right place for me to carry out my plan.

units.source_text: 我扒开竹枝，若有其事的撒谎，说宝贝就在杉树下面埋着呢。

en.t: I pushed aside the bamboo branches and lied with a perfectly serious air, saying that the treasure was buried under the cedar trees.

units.source_text: 我刚说完，男的拔腿就往竹林深处的矮小杉树走去。

en.t: No sooner had I said it than the man hurried off toward the low cedars deep in the bamboo grove.

units.source_text: 那里竹子不多，并排长着几颗杉树——我猝不及防按倒了那个男人。

en.t: There were not many bamboos there, and several cedars stood side by side; catching him off guard, I knocked the man down.

units.source_text: 那人力气似乎很大，不愧是带刀武士。

en.t: The man seemed very strong, just as one would expect of a sword-bearing warrior.

units.source_text: 不过我打他个措手不及，他也是无可奈何。

en.t: But because I had taken him completely by surprise, there was nothing he could do.

units.source_text: 我把他捆在一颗杉树脚下。

en.t: I tied him up at the foot of one of the cedar trees.

units.source_text: 做贼的行当，保不齐什么时候就翻墙入室，我随时都别在腰间的。

en.t: In the thieving trade, you never know when you may have to climb over a wall and break into a house, so I always kept it tucked at my waist.

units.source_text: 是的，我用竹叶堵住了他的嘴，免得他喊叫惹来麻烦。

en.t: Yes, I stuffed bamboo leaves into his mouth so that his shouting would not bring trouble.
